title: Night of the Network Map
premise: A long drama of subway network map design. A-He and A-Wei are easily confused; the network master map goes intact→ink-bled→redrawn; the folding measuring wheel is crushed and must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_on_duty: Subway network designer Lu Heng around thirty-five, neat short hair, deep-blue work shirt with a scale pin on the cuff, fingertips often stained with highlighter ink, sharp gaze.
states.weary_injured: The same Lu Heng weary and injured: work shirt torn at a corner, gauze on the brow, still wearing the scale pin, heavy steps.
states.left_post: Lu Heng has left his post; only his deep-blue old work clothes and badge remain in the drafting room—he himself no longer appears.

states.young_apprentice: Young A-He: a lean drafting apprentice around fifteen, turmeric armband on the left arm, knuckles white when gripping a pen, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Adult A-He: a tall upright successor drafter in his twenties, still in turmeric armband, calm eyes.

states.intact: A full-wall city subway network master map, colored lines crossing, transfer nodes marked with magnets, surface flat unmarked.
states.ink_bled: The same network master map stained by a spilled inkbottle in purple-black blooms; many colored lines smear together, transfer nodes hard to read.
states.redrawn: After redrawing, the network master map's colored lines are clear again, but a shallow patch mark remains at the lower right, apart from the first intact state.

states.intact: A deep-blue leather transfer notebook, pages packed with station-spacing sketches and ridership curves, clean corners.
states.coffee_stained: The same transfer notebook soaked by spilled coffee, cover warped, page writing bled, a crumpled blotter sheet tucked inside.

states.intact: A foldable yellow-and-black measuring wheel, centimeter marks on the rim, handle wrapped in nonslip tape.
states.crushed: The folding measuring wheel crushed by a construction truck, rim split, marks twisted—only a skewed wreck remains.

states.young_rival: A-Wei nearly identical in face and build to A-He, but an amber brooch at the collar, bold and quick to interrupt.
states.disguised: Disguised A-Wei still wears the amber brooch, plus thin-frame glasses, expression deeper.

E18.name: pocket schematic puzzle

segments.action: At dusk, Lu Heng opens the transfer-center drafting room door and sets a T-square on the long table.
A row of five drafting desk lamps is screwed along the long table; Lu Heng lights each and wipes dust inside the shades.
By the window frame hang two copper platform announce bells; Lu Heng taps them with a knuckle, short tones echoing off the whiteboard walls.
Lu Heng rises on tiptoe to check the line width of every transfer color on the network master map.
By the window Lu Heng watches dimming sky light beyond the station-hall glass dome.
The intact network master map covers the whole wall; colored lines gleam faintly under the drafting desk lamps.
With a highlighter Lu Heng adds an unopened branch line on the whiteboard.
Lu Heng unpins and re-pins the scale pin on his cuff, habitually checking the marks.
Lu Heng sorts scattered color cards and reorders them by line number.
Lu Heng sits on a drafting-room tall stool and rubs his aching neck.
Lu Heng opens the deep-blue leather transfer notebook and records today's ridership spot-checks.
In the transfer notebook Lu Heng draws a walking-minutes curve between two stations.
Lu Heng closes the transfer notebook and tucks it into the long-table drawer.
Colored-line gleam from the network master map sweeps Lu Heng's profile.
Against the network master map Lu Heng circles congested transfer points in red.
Lu Heng caps spare highlighters tight so the tips will not dry.
In the morning station-hall mockup zone, Lu Heng greets young A-He pushing the folding measuring wheel in.
A-He steadies the folding measuring wheel and pats cement dust from the rim.
Lu Heng points to three red-and-white transfer-node magnets, teaching A-He which transfer stations each marks.
A-He crouches by unfinished floor tiles, curiously touching temporary station-name stickers on a column.
Lu Heng explains to A-He the scale difference between the mockup zone and a real station hall.
A-He looks back at the intact folding measuring wheel, eyes full of longing.
Lu Heng has A-He push the folding measuring wheel once around the mockup zone and record wheel turns.
A-He cinches the turmeric armband and carefully notes the station spacings Lu Heng dictates.
In the construction corridor, A-Wei with an amber brooch at the collar turns to look from behind a cable reel.

segments.action: On a reroute-week morning, Lu Heng erases old branch-line drafts from the whiteboard.
With cyan-green highlighter Lu Heng redraws a parallel express-line sketch.
Lu Heng presses a T-square along the whiteboard's lower edge to keep the baseline level.
Against the network master map Lu Heng checks crossings of the new express line with the existing loop.
In the afternoon Lu Heng takes a dispatch call in the drafting room, brows slightly furrowed.
On a sticky note Lu Heng writes 'delay opening' and sticks it to a whiteboard corner.
Lu Heng rearranges color cards and pulls the express-line color aside alone.
At dusk Lu Heng switches off spare lamps, leaving only the center one on the network master map.
In the ridership-marking stretch, Lu Heng hangs transparent tracing paper beside the network master map.
With orange dots Lu Heng marks congested morning-peak transfer nodes.
Lu Heng fixes tracing-paper edges with magnetic strips against curling.
Against stained pages in the transfer notebook Lu Heng struggles to read old numbers.
Lu Heng sets a fresh cup of tea farther away, afraid of spilling on the notebook again.
On the whiteboard Lu Heng lists three proposed last-train time adjustments.
Outside the drafting-room window a trial train rumbles; Lu Heng looks up and listens a moment.
With thin cord Lu Heng restrings color cards by line number.
On station-hall patrol day, Lu Heng puts on a hard hat and walks into the station-hall mockup zone.
Lu Heng tests unset tile adhesive with a toe.
Lu Heng notes where column stickers have peeled.
With a flashlight Lu Heng shines into an unpowered sign lightbox.
At the mockup-zone entrance Lu Heng talks briefly with the construction foreman.
Lu Heng skirts stacked cable reels and rounds to the other platform.
With a tape Lu Heng measures reserved fare-gate width.
Lu Heng writes the measurements on a cuff sticky note.
At dawn, Lu Heng patrols the station-hall mockup zone; the folding measuring wheel leans by a column.
Lu Heng crouches to check whether the folding measuring wheel rim marks are worn.
Lu Heng walks to a temporary bench; those three transfer-node magnets are still lined up neat.
A plastic demo cart printed 'For Display' is pushed through the mockup zone—no marked rim, never a folding measuring wheel.
Lu Heng stands in the mockup zone, logging unfinished tile gaps.
Lu Heng pushes the folding measuring wheel to a drier corner and stands it upright.
Lu Heng confirms again that none of the three transfer-node magnets is missing.
On a whiteboard at the mockup-zone exit Lu Heng writes the patrol date.
On the eve of a storm, Lu Heng shelves all drafts near the drafting-room window.
